props.title: A musician DJ in Denver, for weddings and parties.
props.lede: It’s late, the floor is full, and the DJ steps out from behind the decks with a saxophone to play over the chorus everyone knows. A musician DJ plays your whole event as a DJ and picks up a live instrument over the mix a few times through the evening.

headingText.html: It’s one performer, one booking and one setup for a wedding, a company party or a milestone birthday.

props.title: What does a musician DJ do?
props.lede: The performer plays a full DJ set on their own decks, mixer and sound system. A few times through the evening, they pick up their instrument and play live over the mix for fifteen to thirty minutes, then go back to the decks.

props.html: Each performer plays one instrument, such as saxophone, violin, guitar, keys or hand drums, and we match you with the one you’d like to hear. The performer plays live for about a third of your event. The rest of the time, you have a DJ set with your requests and your do-not-play list.
Want a second musician or a full band, too? Take a look at the DJ page or the roster.

props.html: You can add a ceremony set, an extra hour, lighting, or a song the performer learns to play live for you. For a large venue, the performer can play through the venue’s sound system, or we can bring more sound.

rows.term: Weddings, from the ceremony to the last dance
rows.text: With one booking, you have music for the ceremony, the cocktail hour, dinner and the dancing. You keep a DJ’s full request list for the reception and still have a live musician for the moments you care about.
Your team dances to the songs they know, and the performer plays live over the ones they cheer loudest for.
A musician DJ is a great pick for a party at home or a restaurant buyout, where there’s no space for a band.
The performer needs the same floor space and power as a DJ, so you can have live music at a venue where a band won’t fit.

props.html: Wondering what it all costs? Take a look at the cost guide. Still deciding? Here’s our take on band or DJ for a Denver wedding or company party.

props.title: Can I choose what’s played live?
props.lede: Yes. Give us a few songs you’d love to hear on the instrument, and the performer will plan the live passages around them. If there’s a song they don’t play yet, they can learn it for you.

props.html: The DJ set is open format, so the performer plays all kinds of music, and you can mix as many styles as you’d like.

items.q: What instrument does the performer play?
items.a: Each performer plays one instrument, such as saxophone, violin, guitar, keys or hand drums. Tell us what you’d like to hear, and we’ll match you with the right performer.

As loud as your venue allows. The performer keeps the music low during dinner so your guests can talk, then turns it up for dancing. If your venue has a sound limit, let us know and the performer will work within it.

items.q: Does the musician DJ take requests?
items.a: Yes. The performer plays your requests, and guests’ requests when they fit, and works from your do-not-play list.

items.q: How much space does the performer need?
items.a: About the same as a DJ: a table, power nearby and a little space to stand and play. So a musician DJ is a good choice for a venue where a band won’t fit.

props.title: Want a DJ who plays live, too? Send us the date and the venue, and tell us which instrument you’d like to hear.
